_what_this_is: The declared header of every table this repo commits. src/validate.py compares each committed table against its entry here and exits non-zero on any difference, including an ADDED column. This is the person-name control's checking half; the enforcing half is that every writer in src/ emits an allow-list rather than a source's whole row, so a new upstream field cannot arrive in an output at all. Both halves are needed: the writer stops the common case, this stops a writer being changed without the change being noticed.
_why_a_publish_gate_and_not_a_git_hook: The canonical .githooks/pre-commit runs exactly two gates and ends in `exec`; it is marked 'Never edit' and its bytes are hashed by the estate's drift check, so a third gate cannot be chained without creating drift. A PreToolUse hook was considered and rejected: SESSION-RULES rule 3 and the starter kit both record that a PreToolUse gate is handed the index as it stood BEFORE the tool call, so staging and committing inside one call passes a gate that already read the index -- which is precisely why the whitespace check was moved OUT of PreToolUse and into a git hook. Repeating that shape would produce a control that reports success and enforces nothing. So this runs in src/validate.py, which exits non-zero and stops the build. The absence of an extension point in the canonical hook is reported as a build-forward candidate for cascadia-standards, not worked around here.

_content_class.organisation: Names a company, law firm, court or agency -- a party to a public filing, not a person. An eponymous firm name is an organisation.
_content_class.person: Names a natural person. NO COLUMN MAY DECLARE THIS. Its presence in this file is itself a validation failure, so the forbidden class is nameable rather than merely absent.
_content_class.identifier: A key, code or docket number.
_content_class.controlled: A value from a declared vocabulary in data/reference/.
_content_class.free_text: Publisher-authored prose. Permitted only where the publisher's own text cannot name a person.
